topic: How do GEO and LEO constellations trade off coverage area versus latency in 5G NTN architectures?
consensus_response: In 5G NTN architectures, GEO constellations provide vast coverage area but at the cost of significant latency (238 ms one-way), affecting real-time applications. LEO constellations minimize latency (down to 2 ms) but require a large number of satellites (hundreds) for global coverage, increasing operational and maintenance costs and complex resource allocation and interference management challenges. To optimize performance and minimize costs in LEO constellations, advanced resource allocation algorithms and signal processing techniques are being developed to manage the large number of satellites and minimize interference. High-altitude platforms can also provide low-latency communication to high-density urban areas while minimizing the number of satellites required for global coverage.
